mainTopic: Doubts and חזקות in עירוב: contradictions in רבי מאיר and רבי יוסי, the limits of ספק עירוב כשר, and status during בין השמשות
overview: The amud opens with רבא explaining why רבי מאיר is lenient in one doubt about טומאה but strict about a doubtful עירוב: the lenient case has two חזקות, the עירוב case only one. The גמרא then finds a similar contradiction in רבי יוסי and gives three answers. First, טומאה is rooted in the תורה, while for רבי יוסי תחומין are only דרבנן. Second, the lenient ruling is really a tradition he reported from his teacher. Third, רבא says the impure person keeps his חזקה of טומאה, because the מקוה was never measured. A ברייתא then limits ספק עירוב כשר to a doubt about WHEN a known change happened, and the גמרא corrects its wording about produce to a case of mixing. Next come cases about status at twilight. A pure loaf that cannot be identified is no עירוב, because neither loaf can be eaten before שבת. A loaf that is חול today and הקדש tomorrow stays חול at twilight, while the reverse case stays הקדש. Finally, from a משנה about a טבול יום flask, רבא concludes that the עירוב acquires at the end of the day.

steps.title: רבא: Two presumptions there, only one here
steps.stepSummary: רבא resolves the contradiction in רבי מאיר by showing that the lenient case has two חזקות for leniency, while the עירוב case has only one.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: There, there are two presumptions pointing to leniency. Here, there is only one presumption pointing to leniency.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives his own answer to the earlier contradiction in רבי מאיר. He explains why רבי מאיר is lenient in one doubt-case and strict in the other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the case where someone touched a person later found dead, there are two חזקות. The dead person was alive until now, and the one who touched him was טהור until now. With the תרומה used for an עירוב there is only one חזקה, that the תרומה was טהור. One חזקה is not strong enough for רבי מאיר to be lenient, but two are.

keyTerms.meaning: רבא said (here introducing a new answer)
presumption(s): we assume things stay as they were until we know otherwise
toward leniency
there … here (comparing two cases)

phrases.english: Rava said:
There, there are two presumptions for leniency,
phrases.notes: The case of touching someone at night who was found dead in the morning: he was presumed alive, and the toucher was presumed pure.

phrases.english: but here there is only one presumption for leniency.
phrases.notes: Here we're talking about the תרומה used for an עירוב that might be impure. The only thing on our side is the presumption that it was pure.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר: הָתָם תְּרֵי חֶזְקֵי לְקוּלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues earlier: a new answer to the contradiction in רבי מאיר
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases by the number of חזקות
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי מאיר seems inconsistent, lenient in one ספק טומאה and strict in another
steps.terutzMaskana: Two חזקות are enough for leniency; one חזקה is not
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the strength of a ספק can depend on how many חזקות support each side.

steps.title: רבי יוסי seems to contradict himself
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out a contradiction between two rulings of רבי יוסי.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is a difficulty: רבי יוסי contradicts רבי יוסי!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves from רבי מאיר to רבי יוסי and raises a new contradiction. This step sets up the answers that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In our משנה, רבי יוסי says ספק עירוב כשר, which is lenient about a doubt. Elsewhere, about a doubt in טבילה (immersion), he rules strictly. So why is he lenient in one doubt and strict in the other?

keyTerms.meaning: a difficulty or contradiction
רבי יוסי's ruling against רבי יוסי's other ruling

phrases.english: There is a difficulty: Rabbi Yosei against Rabbi Yosei!
phrases.notes: Lenient about ספק עירוב, yet strict about doubts concerning immersion.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Parallels the earlier question on רבי מאיר, now aimed at רבי יוסי
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוסי's lenient ruling of ספק עירוב כשר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: He is strict about a doubt in טבילה, so he should also be strict about a doubt in עירוב

steps.title: Impurity is different because it is rooted in the תורה
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בר חיננא explains that רבי יוסי is strict about טומאה because טומאה has a basis in the תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא בר חיננא said: טומאה is different, since it has a root in the תורה.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא בר חיננא answers the contradiction. Doubts in טומאה are treated more strictly than doubts in עירוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because טומאה as a whole comes from the תורה, רבי יוסי is strict even about a doubt involving a rabbinic level of impurity. עירוב does not have that kind of Torah root, so a doubt there can be treated leniently.

keyTerms.meaning: it is different
ritual impurity
since, because
a basis or root in the תורה

phrases.english: Rav Huna bar Chinnana said:
Impurity is different,

phrases.aramaic: הוֹאִיל וְיֵשׁ לָהּ עִיקָּר מִן הַתּוֹרָה.
phrases.english: since it has a basis in the Torah.

steps.triggerLanguage: שָׁאנֵי טוּמְאָה, הוֹאִיל וְיֵשׁ לָהּ עִיקָּר מִן הַתּוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction in רבי יוסי
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing by source: Torah-rooted versus not
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A doubt is a doubt, so רבי יוסי should rule the same way in both cases
steps.terutzMaskana: Doubts in an area rooted in the תורה (טומאה) are treated strictly

steps.title: But שבת is also from the תורה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the answer: שבת is also דאורייתא, so why be lenient about ספק עירוב?
steps.simpleTranslation: But שבת is also from the תורה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רב הונא בר חיננא's answer. If Torah-rooted laws get strict treatment, שבת should too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An עירוב lets a person walk beyond the תחום on שבת. Since שבת is a תורה law, a doubt about the עירוב should be treated as strictly as a doubt about טומאה. The distinction seems to fall apart.

keyTerms.meaning: also
from the תורה (a law on the level of the תורה)

phrases.english: Shabbat is also from the Torah!?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in step 3
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא בר חיננא's distinction based on Torah origin
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: שבת is also Torah law, so ספק עירוב should be treated strictly too

steps.title: רבי יוסי holds שבת limits are rabbinic
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that according to רבי יוסי, תחומין are only דרבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי holds: the שבת boundaries (תחומין) are rabbinic.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב הונא בר חיננא's answer. The עירוב here deals with תחומין, which רבי יוסי considers a rabbinic law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The עירוב here is an עירוב תחומין. It only matters for the תחום limits, not for all of שבת. Since רבי יוסי holds תחומין are דרבנן, a doubt about them can be lenient, and the distinction from טומאה stands.

keyTerms.meaning: he holds (this is his view)
שבת boundaries: the distance one may walk from one's place on שבת
rabbinic law

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the גמרא is saying שבת itself is rabbinic. Only the specific law of תחומין is rabbinic, and only according to רבי יוסי.
steps.whatToRemember: First answer for רבי יוסי: he is strict about טומאה, which is rooted in the תורה, and lenient about ספק עירוב because, in his view, תחומין are only דרבנן.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei holds:
Shabbat limits are rabbinic.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 4
steps.terutzResolutionType: Clarifying the author's view of the law's source
steps.terutzHavaAmina: ספק עירוב involves Torah-level שבת law
steps.terutzMaskana: For רבי יוסי, תחומין are דרבנן, so leniency in a doubt is fine

steps.title: One ruling is his own, the other is his teacher's
steps.stepSummary: A second answer: the strict ruling is רבי יוסי's own view, and the lenient ruling on ספק עירוב is his teacher's.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you wish, say: this ruling is his own, and that ruling is his teacher's.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a completely different way to answer the contradiction in רבי יוסי. There is really no contradiction, because the lenient view is not his own.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this answer, רבי יוסי's own position is the strict one. The lenient ruling about ספק עירוב is something he reported in his teacher's name, and he may not personally agree with it.

keyTerms.meaning: and if you wish, say (introducing an alternative answer)
his own
his teacher's

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:
This is his own view; that is his teacher's view.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא: הָא דִּידֵיהּ, הָא דְּרַבֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, independent answer to the קשיא in step 2
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attributing the two rulings to different authorities
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both rulings are רבי יוסי's own opinion
steps.terutzMaskana: The lenient ruling is his teacher's, which he only reported

steps.title: The משנה's wording supports the second answer
steps.stepSummary: The wording of the משנה shows that רבי יוסי was quoting אבטולמוס, so the lenient ruling is not his own. The גמרא concludes this is correct.
steps.simpleTranslation: The wording is precise too, because it teaches: רבי יוסי said, אבטולמוס testified in the name of five elders that a doubtful עירוב is valid. Learn from this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings proof from the exact wording of the משנה for the second answer. It then concludes that the proof works.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי did not say 'a doubtful עירוב is valid' in his own voice. He said אבטולמוס testified this in the name of five זקנים. That shows he was reporting a tradition from others, which fits the answer that the lenient ruling is his teacher's view.

keyTerms.meaning: the wording is also precise, meaning it supports this answer
for it teaches
testified in the name of
a doubtful עירוב is valid
learn from it (the conclusion is accepted)

steps.whatToRemember: Second answer for רבי יוסי: the strict ruling is his own, and the lenient ספק עירוב כשר is a tradition he reported from אבטולמוס. The משנה's wording ('he testified in the name of') supports this.

phrases.english: It is also precise, as it teaches:
Rabbi Yosei said:
Avtolemos testified in the name of five Elders
phrases.notes: The phrasing shows רבי יוסי is reporting someone else's ruling.

phrases.english: that a doubtful eiruv is valid —
conclude from this.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the alternative answer in step 6 from the משנה's wording
steps.raayaObject: The claim that the lenient ruling on ספק עירוב belongs to רבי יוסי's teacher
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's phrasing: 'אבטולמוס testified in the name of five elders'
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The contradiction in רבי יוסי is resolved: ספק עירוב כשר is a reported tradition, not necessarily his own view

steps.title: רבא: The impure person keeps his status
steps.stepSummary: רבא gives a different answer to the contradiction: in the מקוה case, רבי יוסי is strict because the person was definitely טמא before, so we assume he is still טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: There, in the מקוה case, this is the reason for רבי יוסי's view: keep the impure person in his known status, and say that he did not properly immerse.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא offers a new way to explain why רבי יוסי is strict about the מקוה but lenient about a ספק עירוב. He says the strictness comes from the rule of חזקה, not from the topic of טומאה itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier answers said the difference was טומאה versus שבת, or רבי יוסי versus his teacher. רבא says the difference is a חזקה: the person was certainly טמא before he went into the מקוה. Since we are unsure whether his immersion worked, we leave him in his old status of טומאה.

keyTerms.meaning: Keep it in its known, earlier status
A presumption that things stay as they were until we know they changed
Immersed (in a מקוה)
There, in that other case

steps.whyThisMatters: This changes the whole explanation. רבי יוסי is not simply 'strict about טומאה.' He follows חזקה, which happens to lead to strictness here.

phrases.english: Rava said:
There, this is the reason of Rabbi Yosei:
phrases.notes: 'There' means the case of the מקוה that was found lacking.

phrases.english: keep the impure person in his presumptive state,
and say that he did not immerse.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר, הָתָם הַיְינוּ טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a third, independent answer to the contradiction, after the answers of רב הונא בר חיננא and the teacher/student answer.
steps.terutzResolutionType: New reason (חזקה) that separates the two cases
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוסי is strict in the מקוה case because טומאה is from the תורה, or because the lenient ruling was not his own.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יוסי is strict in the מקוה case because the person has a חזקה of טומאה. In the עירוב case there is no such negative חזקה.

steps.title: Why not keep the מקוה in its valid status?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבא: the מקוה also has a known status of being valid, so we should assume it still had enough water.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the contrary! Keep the מקוה in its known status, and say that it was not lacking water!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רבא's answer. It points out a חזקה that pulls the other way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If we follow חזקה, the מקוה was full and valid before, so we should assume it was still full when the person immersed. That would make the person טהור. The two חזקות cancel each other out, so רבא's reason no longer explains why רבי יוסי rules strictly.

keyTerms.meaning: On the contrary; just the opposite
A ritual bath, which must hold a set amount of water
Was lacking (the required amount)

phrases.english: On the contrary, keep the ritual bath in its presumptive state,
and say that it was not lacking!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבא's answer by naming a competing חזקה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's claim that the person's חזקה of טומאה decides the case
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The מקוה also has a חזקה of being valid. Following that חזקה would make the person טהור, so חזקה cannot be the reason for the strict ruling.

steps.title: The מקוה was never measured
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the case is a מקוה that was never measured, so it has no earlier status of being valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: We are speaking about a מקוה that was never measured.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבא by narrowing the case. Without a past measurement, the מקוה has no חזקה at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A חזקה needs a known starting point. Since nobody ever checked that this מקוה had enough water, there is no 'valid' status to keep. Only the person's חזקה of טומאה is left, so רבא's answer stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Was measured (checked for the required amount of water)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the מקוה is assumed to be invalid. It simply has no חזקה either way, so it cannot outweigh the person's known status of טומאה.
steps.whatToRemember: According to רבא, רבי יוסי is strict in the מקוה case because of the person's חזקה of טומאה. The מקוה, never measured, has no opposing חזקה.

phrases.english: In a ritual bath that had not been measured.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 9 by limiting the case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The מקוה has its own חזקה of being valid, which cancels the person's חזקה of טומאה.
steps.terutzMaskana: This מקוה was never measured, so it has no חזקה. The person's חזקה of טומאה decides the case.

steps.title: A ברייתא defines a valid doubtful עירוב
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא explains which ספק עירוב רבי יוסי calls valid: food that was fine at one point, where we only don't know WHEN it changed, before or after nightfall.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: In what case did רבי יוסי say that a doubtful עירוב is valid? If someone made an עירוב with תרומה, and there is a doubt whether it became טמא while it was still day or after nightfall. Similarly with produce: if there is a doubt whether it was fixed (tithed) while it was still day or after nightfall. This is the doubtful עירוב that is valid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that spells out exactly what kind of doubt רבי יוסי means when he says a ספק עירוב is valid. It gives two examples.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the תרומה case, the food was definitely טהור earlier and only later became טמא. In the produce case, the food was טבל and later became definitely fixed. In both cases, the food's status is known at some point, and the only question is the timing compared to nightfall, which is the moment the עירוב takes effect.

keyTerms.meaning: An עירוב whose validity is in doubt
The portion given to a כהן; it may be eaten only when טהור
While it is still day, before שבת begins
After it got dark, once שבת began
Were fixed, meaning tithed and made permitted to eat

steps.confusionAlert: The עירוב takes effect right around nightfall. רבא later shows (step 27) that the moment that counts is the very end of the day, before שבת begins. That is why the question 'before or after dark' is so important: the food must be usable at that moment.

phrases.english: It was taught: In what case did Rabbi Yosei say
that a doubtful eiruv is valid?
If one made an eiruv with teruma,
there is a doubt whether it became impure while still day
or whether it became impure after nightfall;
and similarly with produce,
a doubt whether it was rendered fit while still day
or whether it was rendered fit after nightfall —
this is the doubtful eiruv that is valid.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא: כֵּיצַד אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי סְפֵק עֵירוּב כָּשֵׁר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from the contradiction to defining the scope of רבי יוסי's lenient ruling on ספק עירוב.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A ספק עירוב is valid when the food's status is known at some point and the only doubt is whether the change happened before or after nightfall.

steps.title: A doubt from the start is not a valid עירוב
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: if the doubt is about the food's basic status from the beginning, such as whether the תרומה is טהור at all or whether the produce was ever tithed, the עירוב is not valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if someone made an עירוב with תרומה and there is a doubt whether it is טהור or טמא, and similarly with produce, a doubt whether it was fixed or not fixed, this is not the doubtful עירוב that is valid.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes by giving the opposite case. Here, רבי יוסי's leniency does not apply.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In these cases there is no known moment when the food was fine. The doubt is not about timing but about whether the food was ever usable at all. Because nothing certain supports the עירוב, it is not valid.

keyTerms.meaning: But; introduces the contrasting case
Unsure whether it is pure or impure, from the outset
This is not (the case meant)

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוסי's ספק עירוב כשר applies only to a doubt about WHEN a known change happened, before or after nightfall. A doubt about the food's basic status from the start makes the עירוב invalid.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the exact limits of the famous rule ספק עירוב כשר. It is not a blanket leniency for every doubt.

phrases.english: But if one made an eiruv with teruma,
in doubt whether it is pure or impure;
and similarly with produce,
in doubt whether it was rendered fit or not rendered fit —
this is not a doubtful eiruv that is valid.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲבָל עֵירַב בִּתְרוּמָה, סָפֵק טְהוֹרָה סָפֵק טְמֵאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא by giving the contrasting case where the leniency does not apply.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When the doubt concerns the food's basic status from the outset, and not just the timing of a change, the עירוב is not valid.

steps.title: Why treat תרומה and untithed produce differently?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the ברייתא uses the rule 'keep the earlier status' to call the תרומה pure, but does not use the same rule to say the produce stayed untithed.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difference with תרומה? There we say: keep the תרומה in its earlier status and assume it was still pure. Then with produce too, we should say: keep the טבל in its earlier status and assume it was not yet tithed!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the ברייתא from Step 11. It says the ברייתא is not using the 'earlier status' rule the same way in both cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With תרומה, the earlier status was pure, so keeping that status makes the עירוב valid. But with produce that started as טבל, the earlier status was untithed. Keeping that status should make the עירוב invalid, yet the ברייתא seemed to call it valid.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the difference? (a challenge to an unequal ruling)
Keep it in its earlier, known status
Produce from which the required tithes have not been taken; forbidden to eat
They were 'fixed', meaning tithed and made fit to eat

steps.confusionAlert: The same rule, 'keep the earlier status', can give opposite results. It helps the עירוב with תרומה, which started out pure, and hurts it with טבל, which started out untithed. The challenge is that the ברייתא seemed to use the rule only when it helped.

phrases.english: What is different about תרומה,
that he says: keep the תרומה in its presumptive status,
and say it is still pure;
produce too:
keep the טבל in its presumptive status,
and say they were not yet tithed!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ברייתא quoted in Steps 11-12.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's ruling that a doubt about whether produce was tithed before nightfall still leaves a valid עירוב
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If 'keep the earlier status' makes the תרומה pure, then the same rule should keep the produce in its untithed status. That would make the עירוב invalid.

steps.title: Change the case: the produce may have become mixed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא fixes the ברייתא's wording. The case is not about whether the produce was tithed in time. It is about produce that was fine and may have become mixed before or after nightfall.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do not say 'doubt whether they were tithed while it was still day.' Instead say: 'doubt whether they became mixed while it was still day, or whether they became mixed after it got dark.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by changing the wording of the case. Now the produce starts out fine to eat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the new wording, the earlier status of the food is that it was fine to eat. The only doubt is when it got mixed with forbidden food. Keeping the earlier status now says the food was still fine at nightfall, just like the תרומה case.

keyTerms.meaning: Do not say this, rather say that (the גמרא is changing a text)
They became mixed with forbidden food (from מְדֻמָּע, a mixture)
While it was still day, before שבת began
After it got dark, once שבת had begun

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוסי allows a ספק עירוב only when the food definitely started out fine to use. The only doubt must be about WHEN it changed. Both the תרומה case and the corrected produce case fit this rule.

phrases.english: Do not say:
doubt whether they were tithed while it was still day,
rather say:
doubt whether they became mixed while it was still day,
or whether they became mixed after nightfall.
phrases.notes: Food that was fine got mixed with forbidden produce. If that happened by day, the עירוב doesn't work; if after dark, it does.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא תֵּימָא סָפֵק מִבְּעוֹד יוֹם נִתַּקְּנוּ אֶלָּא אֵימָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Textual emendation (changing the wording of the ברייתא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא was about produce that started as טבל, and the doubt was whether it was tithed in time.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is about produce that started out fine and might have become mixed before or after nightfall. So the earlier status supports a valid עירוב.

steps.title: Two loaves, one pure, and nobody knows which
steps.stepSummary: רב שמואל בר רב יצחק asks רב הונא about a new case. There are two loaves of תרומה, one pure and one impure, and someone says 'make my עירוב with the pure one, wherever it is.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שמואל בר רב יצחק asked רב הונא: there were two loaves in front of someone, one impure and one pure. He said: 'Make an עירוב for me with the pure one, wherever it is.' What is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new question about an עירוב. Here one loaf is definitely pure, but nobody can tell which one it is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This doubt is different from the earlier ones. There is no question about whether a pure loaf exists, because one definitely does. The only problem is that nobody can identify it. The question is whether an עירוב can rest on a pure loaf that cannot be picked out.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked him (introduces a question to a teacher)
Loaves of bread
Make an עירוב for me
What is the law?

phrases.aramaic: בְּעָא רַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר רַב יִצְחָק מֵרַב הוּנָא:
phrases.english: Rav Shmuel bar Rav Yitzchak asked Rav Huna:
If there were two loaves in front of him,
one impure and one pure,
and he said: make an eruv for me with the pure one
wherever it is,
what is the law?

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּעָא רַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר רַב יִצְחָק מֵרַב הוּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the topic of ספק עירוב to a new kind of doubt: a pure loaf that cannot be identified.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is an עירוב valid when it is based on 'the pure loaf, wherever it is,' when the pure loaf cannot be identified?

steps.title: The question works even for רבי מאיר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that the question works for both opinions. Even strict רבי מאיר might allow this עירוב, because here a pure loaf definitely exists.
steps.simpleTranslation: The question can be asked according to רבי מאיר, and it can be asked according to רבי יוסי. According to רבי מאיר: maybe he only said his strict ruling there, where there may be no pure loaf at all. But here, there definitely is a pure loaf.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows why this question is a real question for both opinions. It starts by explaining why even רבי מאיר, who is usually strict about a ספק עירוב, might allow this case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר called a ספק עירוב invalid in a case where the תרומה might really be impure, so possibly no valid food existed at all. Here, one loaf is surely pure, so valid food definitely exists. That difference might be enough for רבי מאיר to allow the עירוב.

keyTerms.meaning: The question can be asked according to...
He only said his ruling there, in that specific case
There is not / there is

phrases.english: It can be asked according to Rabbi Meir,
it can be asked according to Rabbi Yosei.
It can be asked according to Rabbi Meir:

phrases.aramaic: עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמַר רַבִּי מֵאִיר הָתָם —
phrases.english: Rabbi Meir only said his strict ruling there,
where there is no definitely pure loaf.
Here, there definitely is a pure one.

steps.triggerLanguage: תִּיבְּעֵי לְרַבִּי מֵאִיר תִּיבְּעֵי לְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning behind the question in Step 15, starting with רבי מאיר's side.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does רבי מאיר's strictness apply only when there might be no pure food at all?

steps.title: The question works even for רבי יוסי
steps.stepSummary: The other side of the question: even lenient רבי יוסי might call this עירוב invalid, because here nobody knows which loaf is the pure one.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or perhaps even according to רבי יוסי, he only said his lenient ruling there. In that case, if the loaf is pure, he knows which one it is. But here, he does not know which one it is.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes explaining the question. It shows why even רבי יוסי, who is usually lenient, might call this עירוב invalid. The next step gives רב הונא's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רבי יוסי's case there was only one loaf, so if it was pure, the person knew exactly where his עירוב was. Here the pure loaf cannot be identified. Not knowing which loaf it is might be a worse problem than not knowing whether the loaf is pure.

keyTerms.meaning: Or perhaps (introduces the other side of a question)
If it is indeed so
He knows it, meaning he can identify it

steps.whatToRemember: The two-loaf question sets two kinds of doubt against each other. רבי מאיר might allow it because a pure loaf surely exists. רבי יוסי might forbid it because nobody can identify the pure loaf.

phrases.english: Or perhaps:
even according to Rabbi Yosei,
he only said his lenient ruling there,
where, if it is indeed pure,
he knows which one it is.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל הָכָא, הָא לָא יָדַע לַהּ?
phrases.english: But here, he does not know which one it is?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposite side of the question begun in Step 16, now from רבי יוסי's view.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does רבי יוסי's leniency depend on being able to identify the pure food?

steps.title: רב הונא answers: the עירוב is invalid for everyone
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא rules that the עירוב made with 'the pure loaf, wherever it is' is invalid according to both רבי יוסי and רבי מאיר. The reason is that an עירוב needs a meal that can be eaten while it is still day, and neither loaf can be eaten.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Both according to רבי יוסי and according to רבי מאיר, we need a meal that is fit to eat while it is still day, and here there is none.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא answers the question from steps 15-17. He says the עירוב does not work according to either opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We cannot tell which loaf is pure, so a person may not eat either one before שבת. Both תנאים agree that an עירוב must be food that is fit to eat before nightfall. That requirement settles the question, so the argument between רבי מאיר and רבי יוסי never comes into play.

keyTerms.meaning: A meal that is fit to be eaten
While it is still day, before שבת begins
And there is none (here it is missing)
We require

steps.whatToRemember: Even if a pure loaf definitely exists, an עירוב fails if the food cannot actually be eaten before שבת.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets a basic condition for every עירוב: the food must be edible before nightfall. Knowing that good food exists somewhere is not enough.

phrases.english: He (Rav Huna) said to him:

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין לְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בֵּין לְרַבִּי מֵאִיר
phrases.english: Both according to Rabbi Yosei and according to Rabbi Meir
we require a meal that is fit (to eat) while it is still day
phrases.notes: Neither loaf may be eaten, because each one might be the impure one.

phrases.english: and here there is none.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: בֵּין לְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בֵּין לְרַבִּי מֵאִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the two-sided question set up in steps 15-17
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The עירוב is invalid according to both opinions, because no loaf can be eaten before שבת.

steps.title: רבא asks about a loaf that becomes הקדש at nightfall
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks רב נחמן about a person who says a loaf is חול today and הקדש tomorrow, and then uses it for an עירוב. Is the עירוב valid?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא asked רב נחמן: If someone says, 'This loaf is חול today and הקדש tomorrow,' and then says, 'Make my עירוב with it,' what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: A new question begins. רבא asks about a loaf that is supposed to switch from regular food to הקדש when the day changes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An עירוב takes effect during בין השמשות, and nobody knows whether that time belongs to today or tomorrow. If the loaf might already be הקדש at that moment, it is forbidden food. So רבא wants to know whether that doubt ruins the עירוב.

keyTerms.meaning: Unconsecrated, regular food that anyone may eat
Consecrated (הקדש), belonging to the Temple and forbidden to eat
Make an עירוב for me with this
What is the law?

steps.confusionAlert: Keep in mind that an עירוב is acquired at בין השמשות, the twilight between day and night. The whole question depends on that unclear moment.

phrases.english: Rava asked of Rav Nachman:
This loaf is unconsecrated today
and tomorrow it is consecrated,
and he said: 'Make an eiruv for me with this' — what is the law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new question about uncertainty during בין השמשות
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the possibility that the loaf already became הקדש during בין השמשות invalidate the עירוב?

steps.title: רב נחמן: this עירוב is valid
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן rules that the עירוב made with a loaf that is חול today and הקדש tomorrow is valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: His עירוב is a valid עירוב.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן gives a short answer: the עירוב works.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He does not give a reason yet. That will come in step 24. For now, we learn only that the doubt about twilight does not cancel the עירוב in this case.

keyTerms.meaning: His עירוב is a valid עירוב

phrases.english: He said to him: His eiruv is a valid eiruv.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבא's first question

steps.title: רבא asks about the reverse case
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks about the opposite case: the loaf is הקדש today and חול tomorrow, and the person uses it for an עירוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone says the loaf is הקדש today and חול tomorrow, and then says, 'Make my עירוב with it,' what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא flips the case around. Now the loaf starts out as הקדש and is supposed to become regular food when the day changes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the loaf becomes חול right at בין השמשות, it would be edible food at the moment the עירוב takes effect. The question is whether the twilight doubt works in our favor here as well.

keyTerms.meaning: Consecrated today, unconsecrated tomorrow (for example, it will be redeemed)

phrases.english: (If the loaf is) consecrated today and unconsecrated tomorrow,
and he said: 'Make an eiruv for me with this' — what is the law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The mirror image of the case in step 19
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is the עירוב valid when the loaf may have become חול during בין השמשות?

steps.title: רב נחמן: this עירוב is invalid
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן rules that an עירוב made with a loaf that is הקדש today and חול tomorrow is not valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: His עירוב is not a valid עירוב.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן gives the opposite answer for the reversed case: the עירוב fails.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At first glance this does not match his answer in step 20, since both cases involve the same twilight doubt. That apparent mismatch sets up רבא's challenge in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: His עירוב is not a valid עירוב

phrases.english: He said to him: His eiruv is not a valid eiruv.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the reversed case with the opposite ruling

steps.title: רבא asks: what is the difference?
steps.stepSummary: רבא challenges רב נחמן: both cases have the same doubt about בין השמשות, so why does one עירוב work and the other fail?
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difference?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא challenges רב נחמן's two answers as inconsistent. He is setting up רב נחמן's explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In both cases, the loaf's status at twilight is uncertain. רבא's point is this: if we are lenient about the doubt in the first case, we should be lenient in the second case too.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the difference? (a challenge to an apparent inconsistency)

phrases.english: What is the difference?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the two rulings as contradictory
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's opposite rulings in steps 20 and 22
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same doubt about בין השמשות exists in both cases, so they should get the same ruling.

steps.title: רב נחמן: a doubt does not change the loaf's status
steps.stepSummary: Speaking half in jest, רב נחמן says the answer is obvious. A doubt cannot bring קדושה onto a loaf that was חול, and a doubt cannot remove קדושה from a loaf that was קדש. In each case the loaf keeps its earlier status during בין השמשות.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: After you eat a כור of salt over it, you will understand. If it is חול today and הקדש tomorrow, a doubt does not bring קדושה down onto it. If it is הקדש today and חול tomorrow, a doubt does not take its קדושה away from it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן explains his two rulings. In both cases, the loaf stays in its original state during the doubtful twilight time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule is that a change of status does not happen out of doubt. We keep the loaf's earlier status, its חזקה. In the first case the loaf stays חול at twilight, so it is edible and the עירוב works. In the second case the loaf stays הקדש at twilight, so it is forbidden and the עירוב fails.

keyTerms.meaning: A כור of salt. 'After you eat a lot of salt over it' is a joking way of saying the matter is easy to see after thinking it through.
Out of doubt, based only on an uncertainty
קדושה comes down onto it
Its קדושה goes away from it

steps.whatToRemember: During the doubt of בין השמשות, nothing changes. A loaf that was חול stays חול, and a loaf that was הקדש stays הקדש. That is why the two rulings come out opposite.
steps.confusionAlert: The two rulings are not inconsistent. Both rest on one rule: keep the earlier status. They come out differently only because the loaves started in opposite states.
steps.whyThisMatters: This uses the same 'keep the earlier status' reasoning that appeared earlier in the סוגיא with the תרומה. It shows how a doubt about timing gets settled in practice.

phrases.english: He (Rav Nachman) said to him:
When you eat a kor of salt over it (you will understand):
phrases.notes: A playful remark: the answer becomes obvious once you think about it.

phrases.english: (When it is) unconsecrated today and consecrated tomorrow,
out of doubt, sanctity does not descend upon it.
(When it is) consecrated today and unconsecrated tomorrow,

phrases.aramaic: מִסְּפֵיקָא לָא פָּקְעָא לֵיהּ קְדוּשְׁתֵּיהּ מִינֵּיהּ.
phrases.english: out of doubt, its sanctity does not depart from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves רבא's challenge by giving the single rule behind both rulings
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows that one principle (keep the earlier status in a doubt) produces opposite results
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The same twilight doubt should lead to the same ruling in both cases.
steps.terutzMaskana: A doubt never changes a status. Each loaf keeps its earlier state during בין השמשות, so the חול loaf works for an עירוב and the הקדש loaf does not.

steps.title: A משנה about a flask that is a טבול יום
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה from elsewhere. A person fills a טבול יום flask from a barrel of untithed מעשר and says the contents will become תרומת מעשר when it gets dark. His words take effect.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in a משנה elsewhere: a flask that is a טבול יום was filled from a barrel of מעשר that is still טבל. The person said: 'This is תרומת מעשר once it gets dark.' His words take effect.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next move. It quotes a משנה from another place so that רבא can draw a lesson from it about when an עירוב takes effect.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The flask is a טבול יום, so it is not fully pure until nightfall. If its contents became תרומה right away, the flask would make them impure. By saying 'once it gets dark,' the person delays the תרומה until the flask is fully pure, and the משנה says this works.

keyTerms.meaning: A flask or jug
Something that was immersed today and is not fully pure until nightfall
Produce from which the required gifts were not yet separated. It is forbidden to eat.
The tenth that the לוי must separate from his מעשר and give to a כהן
When it gets dark

phrases.english: We learned there (in a Mishnah):
A flask that is a tevul yom
phrases.notes: Immersed today and fully pure only at nightfall.

phrases.english: that he filled from the barrel
of tithe that is still tevel,
phrases.notes: Its תרומת מעשר hasn't been separated yet.

phrases.english: and he said: 'This is terumat ma'aser'
'once it gets dark' —
his words take effect.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the discussion of a loaf's status during בין השמשות, the גמרא brings a new source about timing near nightfall and the עירוב.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A designation of תרומת מעשר set to take effect at nightfall from a טבול יום flask is valid.

steps.title: Using the same flask for an עירוב does not work
steps.stepSummary: The same משנה continues. If the person said 'Make an עירוב for me with this,' his words mean nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if he said: 'Make an עירוב for me with this,' he has not said anything.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues quoting the משנה and reaches the key line. Using the flask's contents for an עירוב is not valid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The contents only stop being טבל when it gets dark, because that is when the תרומת מעשר is separated. Before dark, the food is still forbidden טבל, and forbidden food cannot serve as an עירוב. So the עירוב fails.

keyTerms.meaning: Make an עירוב for me with this
He has not said anything. His words have no legal effect.

steps.confusionAlert: The food does become permitted at nightfall. The problem is that it is still טבל during the time that matters for the עירוב.

phrases.english: And if he said: 'Make an eiruv for me with this' —
he has not said anything.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same משנה. It shows that what works for תרומת מעשר does not work for an עירוב.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An עירוב made with food that becomes permitted only at nightfall is not valid.

steps.title: רבא: the עירוב acquires at the end of the day
steps.stepSummary: רבא learns from the משנה that the עירוב takes effect at the end of the day, before שבת begins.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: This shows that the end of the day is when the עירוב acquires.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא draws a conclusion from the משנה. The moment that counts for an עירוב is the last part of Friday, not the first moment of שבת night.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Suppose the עירוב took effect at the start of night. Then the food would already be permitted at that moment, and the עירוב should work. Since the משנה says it fails, the עירוב must take effect at the end of the day, while the food is still טבל.

keyTerms.meaning: This shows / we can learn from this
The end of the day (the last moment before nightfall)
The עירוב acquires the person's Shabbat place

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבא, the עירוב must be valid at the END of Friday. Food that becomes permitted only when night falls is too late.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the exact moment that counts for an עירוב. That timing is central to the cases of uncertain status during בין השמשות discussed just before.

phrases.english: Rava said: That is to say:
the end of the day acquires the eiruv,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבא draws a legal inference from the משנה quoted in steps 25 and 26.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The עירוב acquires at סוף היום, the end of Friday, and not at the start of שבת.
